title: Internal Hom from a finite free sheaf is exact
statement: Let $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be a site with a sheaf of commutative rings (a ringed site) [def-pur-sheaf-hom], let $E$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-module equipped with an isomorphism $E\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ for some integer $r\geq0$, and let $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $0\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,A)\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,B)\to\mathcal H om_{\mathcal O_U}(E,C)\to0$ is exact; under the chosen isomorphism $E\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$, each internal Hom is canonically identified with the corresponding direct sum $A^{\oplus r}$, $B^{\oplus r}$, or $C^{\oplus r}$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (Lemma 20.51.4, case (2)), finite locally free Hom calculation in the proof

proof.text: Construct the canonical comparison by mapping the opposite of the inverse of the chosen free-sheaf isomorphism through the internal-Hom functor, composing with the proved source-library SheafOfModules.homObjFreeIso, and then biproduct.isoCoproduct. Unfold the source comparison and its opposite-biproduct construction to prove that composing this comparison with each finite-sum projection equals homObjMap of the corresponding basis inclusion followed by homObjUnitIso. Applying this morphism equality at U and at a section gives exactly the required basis-evaluation equation.

Prove naturality of the comparison in the target module. Cancel the inverse biproduct-to-coproduct comparison and use biproduct.hom_ext. Each projection reduces to the previous coordinate identity. Sigma.hom_ext shows that coordinate projections commute with Sigma.map. Naturality of homObjUnitIso follows by evaluating a section, and homObjMap_comp_homObjMap combines precomposition and postcomposition. This gives both displayed squares.

Prove short exactness of the finite-sum sequence using the constant-diagram functor followed by colim over Discrete I, for I = ULift (Fin r). The constant-diagram functor preserves limits and colimits. HasBiproductsOfShape.colimIsoLim identifies finite discrete colimits with limits, so colim preserves finite limits as well as finite colimits. Apply ShortComplex.ShortExact.map_of_exact. Sigma.isoColimit and its inclusion identities supply the natural comparison with the chosen coproducts; transport short exactness via ShortComplex.isoMk and ShortComplex.shortExact_of_iso. This argument needs only Finite I, with no nonemptiness condition, and therefore includes rank zero.

The composite of the two internal-Hom sequence maps is zero by homObjMap_comp_homObjMap and S.zero, with the remaining zero-postcomposition identity checked on sections. Form the isomorphism of short complexes from the three canonical comparisons and the two naturality squares. ShortComplex.shortExact_of_iso applied to its inverse transports the finite-sum short exactness to the internal-Hom sequence. Return these comparisons together with the basis-evaluation equality proved in the first step.
